page: Amazon Web Services u7i-8tb.112xlarge is an ultra-high-memory instance belonging to the Gen7 memory-optimized family, engineered on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processors running at a base clock speed of 1.9 GHz. The compute topology provides 224 physical cores and 448 virtual CPUs utilizing symmetric multiprocessing with two threads per core.

The primary architectural distinction of this instance is its massive memory capacity. It incorporates 8192 GB (8 TB) of system RAM, allocating approximately 18.29 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no integrated local NVMe storage and does not feature graphics processing units, relying instead on network-attached storage architectures and dedicated CPU compute. Networking capabilities are anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

From an infrastructure and efficiency standpoint, the u7i-8tb.112xlarge represents a specialized tier designed to consolidate extreme in-memory footprints onto a single system image. Because it foregoes bundled local disks and discrete hardware accelerators, its resource allocation is strictly focused on extreme memory capacity and multi-threaded throughput. Workloads operating on this instance require external network volumes for persistence.

This hardware profile is tailored for large-scale enterprise environments that cannot be distributed easily across clustered nodes. Target use cases include massive in-memory databases like SAP HANA, extensive real-time transactional analytics, high-volume caching layers, and very large memory-bound data science processing workloads.
